files.text:
# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — composite modify_reservation + policy baggage computation + cabin-change doc
- Changes I made (1 line per edit):
  - `tools.py::modify_reservation` (NEW composite WRITE): applies cabin/flight + passenger + baggage changes in ONE call, delegating to the existing primitives. Targets the action-stall cluster (12, 17, 22) where the agent confirmed a multi-step modification then emitted only text.
  - `tools.py::update_reservation_baggages` (in-body computation): derives non-free bags from policy `free=FREE_BAG_ALLOWANCE[membership][cabin]*#pax`, `nonfree=max(0,total-free)`; charges only new paid bags. Targets free-bag miscount (12, 17, 22).
  - `tools.py::update_reservation_flights` (docstring only, body unchanged): clarifies cabin change is allowed for basic economy when segments are unchanged; only segment changes are barred. Targets the wrong "basic economy can't be modified" refusal (17, 22).
- Per change, expected effect + why safe:
  - Composite: gives the mid-tier reader ONE call to complete the whole confirmed change instead of remembering 2–3 writes. Safe because it delegates to unchanged primitive bodies → identical DB effect; reward is DB-based (proven by 8/25 where action_match=False but reward=1.0), so even if a passing task's agent picks it, same DB = same reward (verified equivalence on task 11). Primitives kept exposed (11/40 use them).
  - Baggage computation: NO passing task calls update_reservation_baggages (8=book, 11=flights, 25=book, 40=passengers) → zero blast radius; verified it reproduces gold nonfree/charge for 12 & 17 and generalizes across tiers/cabins.
  - Flights docstring: body untouched, so task 11 (pure basic-economy cabin downgrade, segments unchanged) is byte-identical; the note is consistent with task 11 and corrects the false belief that blocked 17/22.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — seed/baseline iteration; LEDGER has only the baseline row, no prior diffs, empty rejected.jsonl.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: (a) action-stall root cause is the model emitting text instead of a tool call after "yes" — the composite reduces steps but cannot FORCE the call; if RESULT shows 12/17/22 still failing, the next lever is likely NOT another tool but the agent-instruction capability (out of scope here). (b) Task 19 wrong-escalation and Task 37 over-booking need discriminating conditions I judged unsafe to encode this iteration.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, check whether 12/17/22 flipped to pass (did the composite get called?). If the composite was NOT selected, try removing the modify-* primitives behind it ONLY after confirming 11/40 can route through the composite unchanged. Revisit 19 via a transfer-time discriminating guard and 37 only if a safe over-write condition exists.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.333 Δ=-0.067 · fixed={19, 37} · broke={11, 25, 40} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: from empty/seed, ship 3 SAFE code+doc fixes — a composite atomic-write tool for the multi-write action-stall cluster, a policy-derived baggage computation (on a tool NO passing task uses → zero blast radius), and a policy-accurate cabin-change doc note. Not yet scored.
- Key measurement insight for future iterations: **reward is DB-state based, not action-name based** (tasks 8/25 pass with `action_match=False`). This means (1) additive/composite tools that reproduce the same DB state are safe even if the agent switches to them, and (2) the safest place to add strong in-body computation is a tool that no currently-passing task calls — here `update_reservation_baggages`.
- Plateau/stall signal: the recurring root failure is BEHAVIORAL — the mid model emits a text summary instead of a tool call after user confirmation. A composite reduces required calls but does not force the call; if it doesn't move 12/17/22, tools alone may be insufficient for that cluster and the lever should shift to the agent-instruction capability (not editable here).
- What to try next iteration: verify whether the composite was actually selected/called in the re-scored trajectories; if yes but arguments were still wrong, tighten per-arg slot-filling docs; if not selected, consider consolidating (remove primitives behind the composite) after confirming 11/40 route through it unchanged.

files.text:
# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## Iteration cand_0001
- The optimizer prompt says "EMPTY SEED — create the capability from scratch (the directory is EMPTY)", but `tools/tools.py` already contained the full 600-line tau2 default tool surface. That contradiction cost time verifying which was true. Suggestion: derive the "empty seed" banner from the actual artifact state (`is_empty(dir)`) rather than a static flag, or drop it when a seed file exists.
- The dominant failure class here (agent narrates/confirms a change then emits text instead of the write call) is fundamentally an agent-instruction/decoding issue, yet the ONLY editable surface for this candidate is `tools.py`. When a cluster's root cause is provably outside the selected capability's edit surface, it would help to (a) surface that in the FAILURES block so the optimizer doesn't burn the iteration chasing an un-fixable cluster, and (b) allow flagging "needs capability X" back to the framework.
- The tau2 venv (`venv-tau2-custom`) is not on PATH and the default `python3` lacks pydantic/tau2; the verify-the-fix loop only works once you discover that interpreter. A pointer to the exact interpreter for offline tool execution in the optimizer prompt would speed verification.

"""Project adapter — optimize tau2-bench AIRLINE's TOOL SURFACE, delivered DIRECTLY.

The capability is the airline agent's TOOLS ONLY. tau2's system prompt (the airline
policy) is NOT part of it and is never edited: the policy reaches the agent exactly as the
benchmark ships it, while the agent's TOOLS come from the candidate's ``tools/tools.py``,
which this adapter installs into tau2's own airline environment in this process.

  * ``tasks``        -> all 50 tau2 airline tasks (stable, network-free).
  * ``run_trials``   -> ONE ``tau2.run.run_tasks`` call for the whole task x trial grid
                        (the fast path cap-evolve prefers), grouped by ``sim.trial``.
  * ``run_batch``    -> the same call with ``num_trials=1`` (one cap-evolve trial).
  * ``run_target``   -> one task via ``run_batch``.
  * ``score``        -> tau2's OWN reward (``sim.reward_info.reward``), read from what the
                        run stashed — never re-run, so it is deterministic. Feedback is
                        gold-AWARE but gold-SAFE and ARGUMENT-LEVEL.
  * ``apply``        -> overrides the registry's airline env constructor so tau2 builds an
                        ``Environment`` with the CANDIDATE tools and tau2's own policy.
                        Guarded on the CANDIDATE'S SHAPE, and it NEVER raises.
  * ``trajectories`` -> the dir of tau2's native per-eval results (full transcript +
                        reward_info), under the run dir.

Nothing here touches the network at import time, so ``cap-evolve check`` stays offline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

# Sibling helper modules (gateway.py) importable regardless of the caller's cwd.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from cap_evolve import CapabilityAdapter, Rollout, Score, Task

import gateway

DOMAIN = "airline"                # tau2's plain airline domain (in-process environment)
N_PRIMITIVES = 14                 # tau2's airline tool surface, the seed's starting point


def _native_sims_enabled() -> bool:
    """Whether to keep tau2's OWN results.json for this eval (default: yes).

    These are the traces `tau2 view` reads, and reading them is how you learn WHY a
    candidate scored what it scored. A flag you must set to get the feature is a flag
    nobody sets, so the default is ON.
    """
    return str(os.environ.get("CAPEVOLVE_NATIVE_SIMS", "")).strip().lower() not in {
        "0", "false", "no", "off"}


# docs/TAU2_SUMMARY.md row 7: tau2's user simulator sometimes emits ``###STOP###`` in the
# SAME message as reasoning that explicitly plans to continue. That ends the conversation
# early for a reason that measures nothing about the agent, so it is recorded as infra
# noise (an errored rollout the harness EXCLUDES) rather than scored against the tools.
_STOP_LEAK_RE = re.compile(
    r"###\s*stop\s*###.{0,400}\b(?:continue|continuing|wait\s+for|must\s+wait|"
    r"keep\s+(?:going|talking)|not\s+(?:done|finished)\s+yet)\b"
    r"|\b(?:continue|continuing|wait\s+for|must\s+wait|"
    r"keep\s+(?:going|talking)|not\s+(?:done|finished)\s+yet)\b.{0,400}###\s*stop\s*###",
    re.I | re.S,
)


def _leaked_stop_continuation(messages) -> bool:
    """True iff a USER-simulator turn emits ``###STOP###`` next to leaked reasoning that
    plans to continue. Only ``user`` turns are inspected — the simulator's own voice."""
    for m in messages or []:
        if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("role") == "user":
            c = m.get("content")
            if isinstance(c, str) and _STOP_LEAK_RE.search(c):
                return True
    return False


def _shown_metrics(reward: float, reward_info: dict, rollout) -> list:
    """The PRIMARY reward plus shown-only secondaries (never gate accept/reject)."""
    metrics = [{"name": "reward", "value": float(reward), "primary": True, "direction": "higher"}]
